issue_context.title: Services configured with `PrivateNetwork=yes` fail to start in containers
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

git main

### Used distribution

Ubuntu 23.10

### Linux kernel version used

6.5.0-5-generic

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

aarch64

### Component

systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Services configured with `PrivateNetwork=yes` should be able to start inside containers.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

Services configured with `PrivateNetwork=yes` fail to start within containers. Specifically, services configured this way fail when pid1 is attempting to mount a private sysfs for mount namespacing:

```
root@six:~# systemd-detect-virt 
systemd-nspawn
root@six:~# systemd-run -p PrivateNetwork=yes --wait /bin/true

Finished with result: exit-code
Main processes terminated with: code=exited/status=226
Service runtime: 14ms
CPU time consumed: 14ms
root@six:~# systemctl status run-u9.service
× run-u9.service - /bin/true
     Loaded: loaded (/run/systemd/transient/run-u9.service; transient)
  Transient: yes
     Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since Tue 2023-10-10 17:33:23 EDT; 7s ago
   Duration: 14ms
    Process: 144 ExecStart=/bin/true (code=exited, status=226/NAMESPACE)
   Main PID: 144 (code=exited, status=226/NAMESPACE)
        CPU: 14ms

Oct 10 17:33:23 six (true)[144]: run-u9.service: Failed to set up mount namespacing: /sys: Operation not permitted
Oct 10 17:33:23 six (true)[144]: run-u9.service: Failed at step NAMESPACE spawning /bin/true: Operation not permitted
Oct 10 17:33:23 six systemd[1]: run-u9.service: Child 144 belongs to run-u9.service.
Oct 10 17:33:23 six systemd[1]: run-u9.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=226/NAMESPACE

Oct 10 17:33:23 six systemd[1]: run-u9.service: Consumed 14ms CPU time.
Oct 10 17:33:23 six systemd[1]: run-u9.service: Releasing resources...
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create a container for use with systemd-nspawn. I did this on Ubuntu 23.10 using debootstrap to create an Ubuntu 23.10 container, but I don't think it really matters how the container is created.

```bash
sudo debootstrap mantic /var/lib/machines/mantic
sudo machinectl start mantic
sudo machinectl shell mantic
```

2. In the container, follow [the instructions](https://systemd.io/HACKING/) to build systemd from source, and then install it inside the container with `ninja -C build install`.
3. Reboot the container.
4. Enter the container again with `machinectl shell mantic`, and attempt to start any service with `PrivateNetwork=yes`, such as `systemd-localed.service` or `systemd-hostnamed.service`. Or, run a transient service:

```bash
systemd-run --wait -p PrivateNetwork=yes /bin/true
```
